title: Backward with Humble Shame We Look
description: Backward with Humble Shame We Look in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 57, headed “Original sin; or, The first and second Adam, Rom. 5. 12. Psalm 51. 5. Job 11. 4”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Back-ward with hum-ble shame we look On our o-rig-i-nal; How is our na-ture dash'd and broke In our first fa-ther's fall!

lines: Backward with humble shame we look
How is our nature dash'd and broke
To all that's good averse and blind,
But prone to all that's ill
What dreadful darkness veils our mind!
The first young pulse begins to beat
How strong in our degenerate blood
And, mingling with the crooked flood,
Wild and unwholesome as the root
How can we hope for living fruit
What mortal power from things unclean
Who can command a vital stream
Yet, mighty God, thy wondrous love
While Christ and grace prevail above

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
